description: CLI that records a web page loading as an MP4 video laid out as scrolling columns, and places two recordings side by side for before/after comparison. Supports network and CPU throttling so the result resembles a real visit.
rules: The repository is go-loadshow; the command is loadshow.
A recording is a demonstration, not a measurement. Never report a duration from a video as the page's load time, and never compare recordings taken with different settings.
Without throttling the video is misleading. Set --download-mbps and --cpu-throttling explicitly; --cpu-throttling 4 is roughly a low-end phone.
For a before/after, both recordings must use the same --preset, --viewport-width and throttling. juxtapose combines any two videos and cannot tell you they were incomparable.
--output / -o is required for both record and juxtapose, and the file is overwritten.
Chrome or Chromium must be installed. On Linux, H.264 encoding also needs ffmpeg; --codec av1 avoids that dependency.
Recording takes real time, bounded by --timeout-sec (default 30). A long encode is not a hang.
--output-summary writes a Markdown summary of the run; quote that rather than describing the video from memory.
This tool produces no metrics — no Lighthouse score, no Core Web Vitals, no waterfall. Use crux or Lighthouse for numbers.
Release archives keep the v prefix and use lowercase os/arch, e.g. loadshow_v1.6.0_darwin_arm64.tar.gz. There is no darwin_amd64 build; building from source needs cgo.
